## Getting started {#getting-started}

::: {.quick-start}
::: {.quick-start-item}
### If you are enrolled

Open the course space, check this week's release, and join the launch session.
:::
::: {.quick-start-item}
### If you are studying independently

Follow the modules in order and use the checks at the end of each page.
:::
:::

::: {.learning-path}
::: {.path-stage}
**Frame problems and evidence**
Define problems, design algorithms, and check tabular data.
:::
::: {.path-stage}
**Build executable solutions**
Translate algorithms into programs and organise decisions in functions.
:::
::: {.path-stage}
**Integrate and assure results**
Test, validate, and improve a complete solution.
:::
:::

## Modules {#modules}

::: {.module-list}
::: {.module-card}
::: {.module-header}
<div class="module-number">01</div>

::: {.module-heading}
MODULE 1

### Problems and algorithms {.unnumbered .unlisted}

Formulate before you program.
:::

<span class="module-effort">About 12 hours</span>
:::

::: {.module-outcome}
**Outcome:** you can state a computational problem precisely and trace an algorithm that solves it.
:::

::: {.module-grid}
::: {.module-section}
#### You will learn {.unnumbered .unlisted}

- Inputs, outputs, and state
- Pseudocode and flowcharts
:::
::: {.module-section}
#### You will do {.unnumbered .unlisted}

- Trace a booking algorithm by hand
- Design tests at and around a threshold
:::
:::

::: {.completion-check}
**Completion check:** you can explain why an exact-fit request fails a strict comparison.
:::
:::
:::

## What success looks like {#success}

::: {.success-grid}
::: {.success-card}
### Explain

You can say what a result means and what it cannot support.
:::
::: {.success-card}
### Verify

You can choose tests that would reveal a wrong answer.
:::
:::

## Weekly rhythm {#rhythm}

::: {.process-intro}
Each week follows the same three moves, so you always know what comes next.
:::

::: {.rhythm-grid}
::: {.rhythm-card}
#### Launch

A short problem introduces the week.
:::
::: {.rhythm-card}
#### Study

Readings and checks build the ideas.
:::
::: {.rhythm-card}
#### Consolidate

A paper exercise brings them together.
:::
:::

::: {.timeline}
1. Read the problem and write down what you already know.
2. Trace the worked example.
3. Attempt the practice set before opening solutions.
:::

::: {.workload-note}
### Workload

Plan about 12 hours per module, spread over at least three days.
:::

## Support {#support}

::: {.support-grid}
::: {.support-card}
### Questions about content

Ask in the [discussion forum](components.qmd) so that others benefit from the answer.
:::
::: {.support-card}
### Personal circumstances

Contact the [course coordinator](landing.qmd) directly and in confidence.
:::
:::

::: {.tool-grid}
::: {.tool-card .tool-card-wide}
### Python

The reference language for every programming exercise. Any recent version works.
:::
::: {.tool-card}
### Spreadsheet

Used for checking results and communicating them.
:::
::: {.tool-card}
### Paper

Tracing by hand remains the fastest way to find a logic error.
:::
:::
